options.benefits: No new draw; useful binary/domain development evidence and transparent sparse-family estimates.
options.comparability: Only frozen V4 development population; no claim to original compliant final evaluation.
options.leakage_risks: Treating repeatedly reviewed Validation as independent final evidence; relaxing gates after outcomes.
options.limitations: Cannot meet original all-family or failed holdout support policy; family estimates remain imprecise and unit dependence remains.
options.name: Preserve V4 with restricted claims
options.new_version: Dataset unchanged; revised research-claim/evaluation protocol must be versioned.
options.policy_compatibility: Preservation and qualified claims fit shortfall policy, but training remains blocked absent explicit approved scope and evaluation plan.

options.benefits: Independent measurement of sparse families using justified coverage and explicit uncertainty.
options.comparability: Separate report and denominators; never pool with V4 population metrics or rank as the same benchmark.
options.leakage_risks: Challenge examples, seeds or errors feeding training; choosing cases by model success; repeated accept-until-support loops.
options.limitations: Enriched challenge prevalence does not estimate population precision/AP or repair frozen holdout failure. Cannot guarantee plausible support in advance.
options.name: Separately versioned external family challenge evaluation
options.new_version: New challenge-set identifier, manifest, protocol, independent entities/streams and custodian seal; V4 unchanged.
options.policy_compatibility: Explicitly contemplated by Stage 15 shortfall_resolution; requires approval and preregistration before execution.

options.benefits: Can address population/history/opportunity design together and seek all-family coverage under a fresh declared protocol.
options.comparability: New population version and fresh evaluation; original V4 preserved as historical evidence.
options.leakage_risks: Seed shopping or recycling failed evaluation feedback into a claimed untouched benchmark.
options.limitations: Cost, synthetic realism and support remain uncertain; repeated generation is not a scientific remedy by itself.
options.name: Future full experiment
options.new_version: Yes: new experiment, design and fresh holdouts.
options.policy_compatibility: Allowed only through versioned authorization and compatibility declaration, never a silent overwrite.

options.benefits: Retains all three domains and the first draw; uses a separately justified challenge evaluation where current family coverage is sparse.
options.comparability: Two explicitly distinct evidence tracks; separate population and challenge conclusions with no pooled prevalence.
options.leakage_risks: Blending datasets/metrics or tuning to extension outcomes. Freeze extension design and eventual model before evaluation; no developer access to challenge outcomes during selection.
options.limitations: Does not restore the original population-level Final/Independent claim; successful extension adequacy remains unproven.
options.name: Preserved V4 development plus justified independent extension
options.new_version: Versioned extension and research/evaluation protocol; no change to existing V4 bytes.
options.policy_compatibility: Combines the declared preservation/challenge pathway; holdout quarantine and G11 remain in force until a separately approved successor protocol defines eligible claims.

original_policy: Cannot be satisfied by the existing failed sealed support certificates; no gate is relaxed.
recommendation: Option D implemented only through a separately approved Option B challenge protocol; no implementation in Stage 16S. If unchanged original population-wide/full-family final claims are mandatory, choose a new experiment (Option C).
